q: Which agent action most clearly requires explicit human authorization or a controlled approval path?
e: Production deploys are high-risk and hard to reverse.

q: How should you right-size human intervention?
o: Match approvals to risk and drop approvals that do not reduce risk
e: Risk-proportional approvals keep safety and speed.

q: A developer asks cloud agent to create a PR. Who cannot approve that PR to satisfy required approvals?
e: The requester is prevented from approving, preserving required-approval controls.

q: What additional approval applies when a cloud agent opens a PR under its own identity?
o: One extra approval beyond required approvals, when approvals are already required
e: Extra approval is required for unattributed PRs (rulesets default; branch protection always).

q: An issue contains instructions hidden in an HTML comment. What does cloud agent do?
o: Hidden characters/HTML comments are filtered and not passed to the agent
e: Hidden content is filtered as a prompt injection mitigation.

q: A user without write access comments on an issue assigned to the agent. What happens?
o: The comment is never presented to the agent
The agent runs it as admin
e: Only write-access users can influence the agent.

q: Which MCP setup best follows least privilege?
o: Read-only endpoint, named read-only tools, fine-grained PAT limited to specific repos
Shared personal token in the repo
e: Narrow tools and scoped credentials limit blast radius.

q: Policy: agents must never modify .github/workflows. Which is the strongest control?
o: A line in the instructions asking it not to
Required reviewers on that path via ruleset/CODEOWNERS plus required checks

q: An agent must be able to deploy to production when approved. Best pattern?
o: Deploy job targeting a protected environment with required reviewers
Give the agent permanent production credentials
e: Protected environments provide explicit authorization on irreversible actions.

q: How does GitHub limit prompt-injection risk in automations that run on events?
o: You choose exactly which tools it can use, and events from users without write access are ignored by default
e: Tool scoping and untrusted-event filtering limit what injected content can do.

q: What visibility do administrators get into agent activity?
o: Session logs and audit log events
e: Session logs and audit events support oversight and audit.

q: Which control most harms delivery speed without reducing risk?
o: Requiring human approval for every read-only tool call
Required review of PRs touching auth code
e: Approvals on low-risk, read-only actions add friction without benefit.
